reasons: The cited Section 14 does grant Client an unconditional, no-cause exit ('written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement'), with services simply running to the last day of the following month — an effective ~30–60 day notice period with no exit fee, penalty or liquidated damages identified anywhere in the reviewed text. That sits at/within the preferred position and comfortably inside the 60–90 day fallback, so 'compliant' is the correct classification.

Vendor has no mid-term convenience exit: Section 13 fixes a 1-year term with auto-renewal, and TrueLink's only unilateral cut-off (partial termination of Sections 2–3) is cause-based, so neither walk-away trigger (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term; Vendor convenience on <90 days) is engaged mid-term.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is explainable as a phrasing variant — the right is drafted obliquely as TrueLink's continuing service obligation up to the Client-elected termination date rather than as an express 'Client may terminate for convenience' grant — and the rationale expressly acknowledges this, so the heuristic miss does not undermine the substance.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline and no counterparty comment were produced; the original paragraphs are returned unchanged.

Residual shortfalls are correctly noted rather than redlined: absence of an express pro-rata prepaid-fee refund is largely moot given monthly arrears invoicing under Section 5a, and the mutual 30-day (rather than 90-day) non-renewal notice in Section 13 operates only at natural expiry and equally benefits Client, so flagging it would cut back our own flexibility.

The 'Subject to Section 4' carve-out is a genuine open item (Section 4 not in the reviewed text and may contain minimum monthly fees that could function as an exit charge), but it is transparently flagged for confirmation rather than mis-stated, which is acceptable for internal evidence.
